articles.title: 엔비디아, 월드 모델 '코스모스 3' 오픈 출시…"피지컬 AI 개발 주기 획기적 단축"
articles.body:
NVIDIA has unveiled Cosmos 3, an open-source world model designed for physical AI development in robotics, autonomous vehicles, and smart spaces.

Cosmos 3 represents "the world's first complete open omnimodel" capable of understanding and generating text, images, video, audio, and behavioral data simultaneously. The system integrates vision reasoning, world generation, and action prediction into a unified framework.

The architecture features two core components: a Reasoner Tower that analyzes diverse inputs to understand object movement and physical interactions, and a Generator Tower that produces future scenes and actions. This consolidation "dramatically shortens development cycles" by reducing what previously required months of simulation and validation to just days.

NVIDIA offers two versions: Cosmos 3 Nano (16 billion parameters) for workstation-level real-time inference, and Cosmos 3 Super (64 billion parameters) for datacenter environments handling complex physics reasoning.

The model achieved top rankings on the Artificial Analysis leaderboard for both text-to-image and image-to-video categories among open-weight models. NVIDIA has made model weights, training code, datasets, and deployment tools available through Hugging Face.

NVIDIA launched the Cosmos Coalition with Agile Robots, Black Forest Labs, Runway, and Skild AI. Samsung, LG Electronics, Li Auto, and Doosan Robotics have officially confirmed intention to integrate the tool.

articles.title: 엔비디아, 'RTX 스파크' 칩으로 애플·인텔에 도전..."데이터센터 넘어 PC까지"
articles.body:
Nvidia announced its new PC platform "RTX Spark" at Computex 2026 in Taiwan, marking its entry into the personal computer market traditionally dominated by Apple, Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm. CEO Jensen Huang declared the company is "reinventing the PC after 40 years."

The RTX Spark integrates Nvidia's Blackwell RTX GPU with Grace CPU on an ARM-based Windows platform, co-developed with MediaTek and manufactured by TSMC. The top-tier RTX Spark Super chip features up to 20 ARM CPU cores, 6,144 CUDA cores, 128GB LPDDR5X memory, and 300GB/s memory bandwidth — capable of handling 120-billion parameter AI models and 1-million token contexts locally.

Nvidia collaborated with Microsoft over three years to redesign Windows as an AI agent platform. The system emphasizes natural language commands with AI agents autonomously managing applications and tasks.

Launch partners include Dell, HP, Lenovo, ASUS, and MSI, with Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra also featuring the chip. Nvidia expects over 30 notebook models and 10 desktop variants at launch, scheduled for fall 2026.

Nvidia also redesigned Adobe Photoshop and Premiere Pro for RTX Spark optimization, with full GPU acceleration and AI-native capabilities.

Beyond RTX Spark, Nvidia also unveiled a roadmap: Vera Rubin Spark (with LPDDR6) and Rosa Feynman Spark follow in subsequent generations.

articles.title: 엔비디아, 중국 유니트리와 휴머노이드 표준 협력...미국 제재 충돌 우려도
articles.body:
Nvidia has partnered with Chinese humanoid robot firm Unitree to unveil a standard humanoid platform for universities and research institutions. However, growing security concerns from US policymakers about Unitree present potential future conflicts with American regulations on China-related technology collaboration.

At Computex 2026 in Taiwan, Nvidia announced the "Isaac GR00T Reference Robot," a standardized platform for academic researchers. The system integrates Unitree's 1.8-meter H2 humanoid robot with tactile sensors from Singapore-based Sharpa and Nvidia's AI computational platform.

The robot features Nvidia's latest AI chips and software, including the Blackwell-based computing system and Jetson Thor processor, enabling on-device AI inference and enhanced autonomous capabilities. CEO Jensen Huang stated: "This platform integrates our entire software stack...making it accessible to all researchers."

Adoption commitments came from Stanford Robotics Center, UC San Diego's robotics lab, AI2, and ETH Zurich. The initiative emphasizes robot security through Secure Boot and Confidential Computing technologies to prevent malware and unauthorized data access.

Despite plans for partnerships with US, European, and Korean manufacturers, Reuters noted potential political backlash. Some US lawmakers have proposed legislation banning federally-funded research institutions from using Unitree robots, citing alleged connections between Unitree and Chinese government/military entities.

Nvidia views the physical AI market as a multi-trillion-dollar opportunity, with Huang projecting rapid sector growth over the next five years.

articles.title: 앤트로픽, EU와 '미소스' 접근 권한 제공 합의..."미국 독점 해제"
articles.body:
Anthropic has agreed to provide the European Union access to Mythos, its cybersecurity AI model, marking the first instance this technology extends beyond the United States and United Kingdom.

According to CNBC and other sources, the EU and Anthropic are currently negotiating detailed conditions for Mythos implementation. The European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA) confirmed ongoing discussions, with final agreements remaining on access rights and operational procedures.

The EU Commission recently visited San Francisco to negotiate with Anthropic. The EU seeks participation in Anthropic's cybersecurity initiative, "Project Glasswing," to detect security vulnerabilities and strengthen defense capabilities across European critical systems.

EU Commission spokesperson Tomas Renié stated: "We've held multiple productive meetings and welcome recent progress regarding potential access rights."

Previously, Mythos had been restricted to select U.S. companies and institutions through Project Glasswing, including Microsoft, Apple, JPMorgan Chase, and CrowdStrike. The UK government remains the only non-U.S. entity with access through its AI Safety Institute.

This agreement reflects shifting U.S. policy on advanced AI model sharing, as the EU has pressured for access for months. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has emphasized the technology should protect democracy and security, not facilitate authoritarianism or surveillance.

Claude Mythos Preview can not only detect software vulnerabilities but also autonomously develop exploit chains at unmatched speed and scale, which has raised concern among officials.

Anthropic plans broader public release of Mythos-level models within weeks pending security protocol completion.

articles.title: 인텔 "에이전틱 AI 시대, CPU 중요성 다시 커진다"
articles.body:
At Computex 2026, Intel formally launched its Xeon6+ server processor, targeting environments requiring large-scale core operations such as cloud services, telecommunications, and agentic AI. The processor addresses shifts in data center workloads away from generative AI model training toward inference using proprietary AI models.

During a panel discussion featuring Intel's Keivolk Ketchyan and industry experts, participants emphasized that CPU importance is expanding in AI processing. CPUs now orchestrate network resources, storage, memory, and GPU utilization — making powerful processors essential for managing diverse AI agents.

According to panelists, agentic AI development requires substantial computing resources beyond simple pre-training. Major AI companies increasingly invest in reinforcement learning and large-scale sandbox environments where CPUs build the operational infrastructure for AI agents.

Ericsson's Magnus Everbrink noted that 'the digital ecosystem will comprise AI, cloud, and mobile networks as three pillars,' with telecommunications carrying AI services. Ericsson projects mobile traffic will increase 10–15 times over the next decade, making power efficiency and scalability critical for telecom operators.

Panelists identified Xeon6+'s high core density and rack-level throughput as key advantages, enabling more AI agents within equivalent power budgets while freeing additional power for GPU allocation. The industry is shifting evaluation metrics from raw core counts toward agent density and power efficiency per rack.

articles.title: Qualcomm CEO says AI agent era has arrived with Dragonfly data center platform
articles.body:
Qualcomm introduced 'Dragonfly' as its dedicated brand for data center products at Computex 2026, advancing its presence in the AI infrastructure sector. CEO Cristiano Amon made the announcement during Computex 2026 in Taipei, noting collaboration with hyperscalers for industrial-scale deployments.

The Dragonfly platform encompasses three product categories: CPUs, AI inference accelerators, and ASICs. The AI accelerators — AI200 and AI250 chips — were introduced in October 2025. The AI200 includes 768GB of LPDDR memory, while the AI250 features near-memory computing architecture designed to improve memory bandwidth tenfold and reduce power consumption. These accelerators are projected to reduce power usage 35–70% compared to conventional GPUs.

Qualcomm signed supply agreements with Humain and plans to support the construction of a 200-megawatt data center starting this year. Revenue generation has been accelerated from fiscal 2028 to fiscal 2027.

The company expects to ship its first ASIC product later this year to ByteDance — a multi-generation collaboration incorporating Alphawave Semi technology for high-speed data transfer.

Qualcomm also announced Dragonwing IQ10 Robotics Reference Design for humanoid robot development, and the Snapdragon C platform for sub-$300 laptops.

CEO Amon declared 2026 as the 'Year of the Agent,' with token demand projected to reach over 4 quintillion per year by 2030 — 40x current levels.

Additional Dragonfly product details will be revealed at Qualcomm's Investor Day on June 24 in New York.

articles.title: KOSPI Aims for 9,000 on Jensen Huang Effect, Tech Giants Surge in Pre-Market
articles.body:
The KOSPI surged more than 2% in pre-market trading Tuesday, building on its previous all-time high of 8,788.38 — just 211 points away from the 9,000 threshold. Momentum came from overnight U.S. tech gains and anticipation surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Korea visit and corporate meetings.

Samsung Electronics traded at 367,000 won (up 5.16%), while SK hynix reached 2.412 million won (up 2.07%) in early trading. Stocks linked to Huang's activities surged sharply: LG Electronics jumped 16.82%, SK Telecom rose 17.38%, Naver gained 8.47%, and Doosan climbed 7.54%.

U.S. markets closed at record highs after initial volatility over U.S.-Iran ceasefire talks. The Dow gained 0.09%, the S&P 500 rose 0.26%, and the Nasdaq advanced 0.42%. Nvidia surged 6.26% following its joint AI PC chip announcement with Microsoft.

Securities firms raised outlook targets. Daishin Securities elevated Samsung and SK hynix targets to 560,000 won and 3.4 million won respectively, citing 'an environment where investors can afford to be bolder.'

Analysts cautioned against extreme market concentration. The KOSPI jumped 33.2% since May while KOSDAQ plunged 11.9%. One analyst noted 'narratives — not macro factors or earnings — drive share prices' currently, recommending a barbell strategy combining semiconductor holdings with overlooked sectors.

articles.title: "시총 1조달러 축하" 엔비디아·SK하이닉스, 차세대 AI 인프라 협력 강화 [GTC 타이베이]
articles.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won met on June 1 during GTC Taipei 2026 to celebrate SK Hynix's recent achievement of reaching a $1 trillion market capitalization.

Huang emphasized the importance of HBM performance, quality, reliability, and supply capacity, stating: 'We must work closely with SK because all of these factors matter for HBM supply.'

During his keynote address, Huang announced that the next-generation Vera Rubin platform entered full production, incorporating TSMC's 3-nanometer process and HBM4 from Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung.

SK Hynix currently commands 50-60% of the global HBM market share. The company began mass production of 4th-generation HBM3 for Nvidia's H100 GPU and achieved world-first 12-stack HBM3E production in 2024. HBM4 development completed in September 2025.

Both executives are strengthening their partnership as a long-term collaboration in AI infrastructure development. SK Hynix exclusively supplied HBM3 to Nvidia's H100 GPUs beginning in 2022, and became the first to mass-produce 12-stack HBM3E in 2024.

articles.title: 엔비디아-SK하이닉스, 차세대AI 인프라 협력 강화
articles.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won met on June 1 during the GTC Taipei 2026 event. The meeting commemorated SK Hynix's recent achievement of surpassing $1 trillion in market capitalization.

Chey attended Huang's keynote address to observe cutting-edge AI technology developments. SK Hynix emphasized that 'the executives shared the significance of the $1 trillion milestone' and affirmed their commitment to 'opening new horizons in AI infrastructure together.'

During a Korea Partner Night event, Huang noted SK Hynix's recent stock performance positively. He stated that 'performance, quality, reliability, and supply capacity all matter for HBM provision,' emphasizing the necessity for close collaboration with SK.

SK Hynix currently holds 50-60% of the global HBM market share as Nvidia's primary supplier. The company exclusively supplied HBM3 to Nvidia's H100 GPUs beginning in 2022, and became the first to mass-produce 12-stack HBM3E in 2024. HBM4 development completed in September last year.

The partnership is expanding into a long-term strategic alliance for the AI infrastructure era. Vera Rubin's production incorporates HBM4 from Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron.

articles.title: 젠슨 황 "베라 루빈 본격 양산"… 삼전·닉스 콕 집어 탑재 선언
articles.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced full-scale production of 'Vera Rubin,' a next-generation AI infrastructure platform, at GTC Taipei 2026 on June 1 local time. Huang stated that while 'all previous CPUs were made for humans, Vera is designed for AI agents.'

The Vera Rubin platform integrates GPUs, CPUs, networking, memory, and software for AI infrastructure. Huang directly named SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, and Micron as HBM4 suppliers, with Vera Rubin expected to feature HBM4 components.

Nvidia officially entered the AI PC market, unveiling the 'RTX Spark' platform based on the MediaTek-developed 'N1 X' system-on-chip. Huang remarked that 'future PCs will become AI assistants working on users' behalf rather than devices awaiting commands.'

Samsung and SK Hynix LPDDR5X memory are expected in N1 X processors. Beyond data centers and personal devices, Nvidia identified 'Physical AI' — enabling robots and autonomous vehicles to understand and control physical systems — as the next growth pillar.

During his upcoming Korea visit, Huang plans sequential meetings with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, LG Group Chairman Koo Kwang-mo, Naver Chairman Lee Hae-jin, and Hyundai Motor Group Chairman Chung Euisun, with discussions expected at a Seongsu-dong Korean BBQ restaurant and Naver's '1784' innovation space.

articles.title: Watch Intel's Computex 2026 keynote here — CEO Lip-Bu Tan takes the stage in Taipei at 10:30pm PT on June 1
articles.body:
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan delivered his keynote at Computex 2026 on June 2 at 1:30 PM Taiwan time, covering Intel's announcements spanning AI PCs, data center CPUs, and AI GPUs.

Key Intel Announcements at Computex 2026:

1. Xeon 6+ 'Clearwater Forest': Intel's first 18A (1.8nm-class) data center CPU, featuring up to 288 Darkmont E-cores, 576 MB L3 cache, 12-channel DDR5-8000, 96 PCIe 5.0 lanes. Intel claims 30% better performance per thread than AMD EPYC 9965. TDP range: 330–450W. SKUs: 144 to 288 cores. Immediately available.

2. Crescent Island GPU: Intel's Xe3P-architecture inference accelerator 'built for agentic AI.' Up to 480GB LPDDR5X memory — bypasses HBM supply constraints. PCIe add-in card at 350W. Launch H2 2026. Supports FP4 through FP64.

3. E835 Ethernet networking platform: 200G Ethernet for AI data center interconnect.

4. AI PC: Intel Arc G-Series for handheld market, Core Ultra Series 3 for edge AI robotics.

The keynote reinforced Intel's resurgence narrative: 18A process is now in data center production, the first such external validation of Intel's advanced node. Intel also previewed Xeon 7 'Diamond Rapids' on 18A-P for 2027.

Tan's keynote emphasized heterogeneous computing and open ecosystems, noting 'the era of just adding more compute is ending — integration and efficiency matter now.'

articles.title: 젠슨 황 "베라 루빈 본격 생산 단계"…삼성·SK하닉 메모리 탑재 [컴퓨텍스2026]
articles.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced production rollout of the next-generation 'Vera Rubin' AI platform at GTC Taipei 2026. Huang stated the platform was 'designed for AI agents' rather than traditional CPU purposes, positioning it as infrastructure optimized for the AI era.

Huang explicitly named SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, and Micron as suppliers for HBM4 (next-generation high-bandwidth memory). Industry analysts interpret this public acknowledgment as confirmation of these companies' status as 'core partners' in Nvidia's AI ecosystem.

The transition from HBM3E to HBM4 is expected to dramatically increase capacity and bandwidth. As Vera Rubin production scales, demand for advanced memory will surge, potentially extending the 'AI memory supercycle' longer than previously anticipated.

Nvidia introduced the RTX Spark platform with MediaTek, integrating CPU, GPU, and memory into unified chips for AI PCs. Samsung and SK Hynix's LPDDR5X memory is likely to power these devices, expanding AI benefits beyond data centers into consumer computing.

The announcement highlighted Physical AI applications — robots, autonomous vehicles, and factory automation. SK Telecom's use of Nvidia's Omniverse platform in SK Hynix chip manufacturing exemplifies expanding AI adoption across manufacturing sectors.

Huang is scheduled to meet with SK Group's Chey Tae-won, LG's Koo Kwang-mo, Hyundai Motor's Chung Euisun, and Naver's Lee Hae-jin to discuss collaboration opportunities in data centers, robotics, autonomous driving, and digital twin technologies.

articles.title: [컴퓨텍스 2026] 아닐 난두리 인텔 "AI 인프라, 더 넣는 시대 끝났다…제온6+·18A로 효율 승부"
articles.body:
Intel executive Anil Nanduri, VP of Data Center Group AI Products and GTM, outlined a shift in how AI infrastructure should be designed at Computex 2026. Rather than continuously adding more computing power, the industry must now focus on efficiency through heterogeneous computing — combining CPUs, GPUs, specialized accelerators, and networking optimized for specific workloads.

Nanduri stated that 'the era of just adding more computing resources has ended' due to supply constraints and rising costs. Success now depends on integrating diverse components effectively.

Intel's competitive advantages at Computex 2026:
- Xeon 6+ processors (Clearwater Forest): Designed to handle orchestration, code execution, verification, and API calls in agentic AI environments. Features up to 288 E-cores on 18A process.
- Intel 18A process technology: Provides manufacturing independence from TSMC bottlenecks, now in data center production.
- Ethernet solutions (E835): 200G Ethernet addresses network bandwidth needs across various performance tiers.

The infrastructure market will move away from single-vendor dominance toward collaborative ecosystems, with hybrid cloud-local deployment models becoming standard.

Nanduri emphasized that Crescent Island GPU — with its 480GB LPDDR5X memory — is positioned as a more cost-effective inference solution than HBM-based alternatives, particularly for enterprises facing memory supply constraints.

articles.title: [단독] 라이칭더 대만 총통, 컴퓨텍스 찾는다…AI 공급망 직접 점검
articles.body:
Taiwan President Lai Ching-te will attend the opening of Computex 2026 at Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center to inspect major tech company booths including ASUS, Foxconn, and MediaTek.

The president plans to examine 'AI semiconductor and server technology, network infrastructure, and robotics developments' while meeting with key corporate executives. His visit underscores Taiwan's position as a 'global semiconductor supply chain hub in the AI era.'

The government is leveraging this event to showcase national competitiveness amid intensifying US-China technology competition. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are also exhibiting, creating potential engagement opportunities between Taiwanese and Korean companies.

This year's theme is 'AI Together,' focusing on AI computing, robotics, smart mobility, and next-generation technologies. The event features over 1,500 companies from 33 countries across more than 6,000 booths — making it the largest Computex on record.

Analysts note that Computex 2026 marks a strategic inflection point: the show has transformed from a consumer electronics trade fair into the world's premier AI hardware and semiconductor showcase, with implications for global supply chain alignment and national technology policy.

articles.title: Marvell CEO calls connectivity the next AI bottleneck, as Nvidia's CEO proclaims Marvell the 'next trillion dollar company'
articles.body:
Data Center Dynamics coverage of Marvell's Computex 2026 keynote on June 2, 2026. Marvell CEO Matt Murphy delivered a keynote titled 'The Future of AI Scaling Depends on Connectivity' at Computex 2026 in Taipei.

Murphy outlined Marvell's transformation from a fast-follower company to a data center connectivity leader. He emphasized that 'connectivity will be the next big bottleneck in datacenter design,' following compute and memory bottlenecks. The company has invested approximately $36 billion in its data infrastructure platform and quadrupled revenue since 2016.

A key announcement was the unveiling of Marvell's new Teralynx T100 switch — the industry's first 102.4 Tbps switch purpose-built for AI, built on 3nm process. At under 1,000W typical power, the T100 delivers up to 25% lower power than competitive solutions. For scale-out deployments, the T100 supports up to a 512-port radix, enabling operators to consolidate network tiers.

NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang joined Murphy on stage to discuss their partnership, highlighting how NVLink Fusion enables heterogeneous data center designs combining custom and semi-custom chips. Huang noted that 'agents are driving the demand for connectivity due to their disaggregated nature.' Huang described Marvell as the 'next trillion dollar company.'

Murphy discussed the transition from copper to optical connectivity, introducing the concept of the 'copper wall' — the maximum distance copper can viably operate before optical solutions become necessary. Murphy concluded by envisioning future disaggregated server architectures where optical connectivity eliminates distance constraints, allowing compute and memory resources to be pooled independently across vastly larger scales.

Marvell completed its acquisition of Celestial AI in February 2026, accelerating its silicon photonics strategy. The NVIDIA-Marvell NVLink Fusion partnership was announced in March 2026, with NVIDIA investing $2 billion in Marvell.

articles.title: Computex 2026: How Nvidia and Qualcomm Are Splitting the Map for the Agentic AI Era
articles.body:
CommonWealth Magazine's analysis of how NVIDIA and Qualcomm are dividing the agentic AI computing market at Computex 2026.

NVIDIA's strategy focuses on data centers and AI factories. At GTC Taipei, Jensen Huang confirmed Vera Rubin full production, RTX Spark for AI PCs (targeting cloud-connected always-on agentic experiences), and Cosmos 3 for physical AI robotics.

Qualcomm's Cristiano Amon positioned Qualcomm in 'distributed AI' — on-device AI reducing cloud dependency. The Snapdragon platform handles on-device inference across smartphones, PCs, and robotics. Dragonfly targets data center inference with 35–70% lower power than GPU alternatives.

Key contrast: NVIDIA wants maximum token throughput at data center scale. Qualcomm wants to distribute intelligence across the edge, reducing the token load on central infrastructure.

Both companies agree on 'Year of the Agent' as the computing paradigm. Qualcomm projects token demand reaching over 4 quintillion annually by 2030 — a 40x increase from 2026 levels.

For Taiwan's supply chain: NVIDIA drives CoWoS advanced packaging demand at TSMC, benefiting SK Hynix and Samsung (HBM). Qualcomm drives LPDDR5X demand for on-device AI, benefiting different memory segments.

The article notes that NVIDIA's data center dominance and Qualcomm's edge AI expertise represent complementary rather than purely competing visions — but the battle for AI PC market share, where both RTX Spark and Qualcomm's Snapdragon X compete, remains a direct confrontation.
